info.title: MICROSERVICE_PROD_Health Monitoring API
info.description: The Health Monitoring API provides real-time status information for the microservices ecosystem. By leveraging this endpoint, users can check the current health and operational status of the underlying services. This API is essential for system administrators or DevOps teams who need to ensure service reliability and uptime. It allows for proactive monitoring and rapid response to any potential issues within the service architecture.

get.summary: Check the health status of the service.
get.description: This endpoint allows you to verify the operational status of the service. A successful response indicates that the service is running smoothly and is ready to handle requests.

requestBody.description: This request body is used to assess the health status of the service. It may include additional parameters to specify the type of health check to be performed, although in this case it is primarily a placeholder to prepare for potential extension of health check options in the future.

200.description: The system is operational and responding as expected.

CheckHealthStatusRequest.description: This schema represents the request body for the health operations GET request in application/json format.

CheckHealthStatusResponse_200.title: Health Check Response

status.description: The current health status of the service.

timestamp.description: The timestamp when the health check was performed.

CheckHealthStatusResponse_200.description: Response schema for a health check operation, indicating service status and related metadata.

HealthCheckMetadata.title: Health Check Metadata

correlationId.description: Identifier to trace the request across services.

generatedAt.description: The timestamp when the metadata was generated.

processingRegion.description: Region where the health check was processed.

HealthCheckMetadata.description: Metadata related to the health check response.

bearerAuth.description: This security scheme uses the HTTP Bearer authentication mechanism. Users must provide a valid JSON Web Token (JWT) to access secured endpoints.
